data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A small research team should adopt an existing experiment tracker only if their workflow is purely observational; however, if the research involves active learning loops where experimental parameters are dynamically adjusted by algorithmic feedback, they must build a custom minimal tracker to serve as the causal controller, thereby avoiding the 'integration tax' of forcing a passive logging tool to act as an active state machine.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The team lacks the engineering bandwidth to maintain even a minimal custom state machine.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The active learning loop operates on timescales slow enough that external API latency from a wrapped tool is negligible.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"An existing tool already exposes native hooks for bidirectional parameter modification without schema translation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Causal Control Boundary: Existing tools function as passive observers (logging state), whereas active learning requires the tracker to be the causal agent (modifying state). Bridging this gap with wrappers introduces latency and schema mismatches ('integration tax') that destabilize the control loop. A custom builder enforces a strict mechanist model where the tracker's architecture mirrors the causal graph of the experiment itself.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
